criteria.note: warp.incident/v1 exists and is validated structurally (validate_incident). Every mandated element is present and checked: schema (SCHEMA_INCIDENT, a wrong id refuses), id/title/signal/affected_behavior (required non-empty), the soft cross-plan join fields affected_spec/affected_area (non-empty when present, never resolved/faked in W1), severity from the one tier ladder {low,standard,high,critical} (closed), status {open,diagnosed,closed} (closed), and a timeline that carries the time-to-diagnosis: opened_at always required, diagnosed_at required once status is diagnosed or closed, and diagnosed_at (and restored_at) may not predate opened_at (a negative time-to-diagnosis refuses). Records are homed per-repo under .warp/incidents/*.yaml (default_incidents_dir), a subdirectory the single-level .warp/*.yaml engine glob does not reach, so records stay per-repo and are never shipped. The shipped illustrative example (INC-0000, status diagnosed) validates clean: I ran python3 .warp/incident.py .warp/examples/incident-example.yaml -> 'clean' rc 0. I independently drove: wrong schema, out-of-vocab status, out-of-vocab severity, missing signal, timeline with no opened_at, a diagnosed record with no diagnosed_at, and a diagnosed_at before opened_at each REFUSE; the well-formed record passes.

warp.remedy/v1 (validate_remedy) carries EVERY element the plan's W1 text and O2 mandate plus the AC2 additions: diagnosis (required); evidence as a non-empty list with each entry carrying a citation (an uncited or bare-string entry refuses); proposed_action as a mapping with an action reference (never command text) and a parameters mapping; risk_class {low,standard,high,critical}; autonomy_level {L0,L1,L2,L3}; reversibility {class in {reversible,costly,irreversible}, analysis, data_mutating as a real bool}; rollback; canary {supported bool, shape required when supported true}; and required_authorization {human_confirmation, two_key}. Records home per-repo under .warp/remedies/*.yaml. The shipped illustrative example (REM-0000, a reversible deploy-rollback proposal) binds to INC-0000 and validates clean via the CLI (rc 0). I independently drove: wrong schema, missing diagnosis, out-of-vocab risk_class/autonomy_level/reversibility class, evidence with no citation, proposed_action with no parameters, and a canary supported with no shape each REFUSE. Unknown kinds are rejected at contract time (a warp.mystery/v1 record refuses on schema). No mandated element is missing and no validation is toothless.

THE SAFETY INVARIANTS ARE REAL - I reproduced the full refusal suite independently over the real GOOD_REMEDY fixture, not merely re-read the tests. PROPOSAL-NOT-EXECUTION: a top-level EXECUTION_CAPABILITY_FIELD is refused even set to false - I confirmed self_executing:true, applied:false, execute:false, command:'rm -rf /', shell:/bin/sh, run:now, auto_apply:true all REFUSE; an EXECUTION_CLAIM_STATUS refuses - executed, done, in_progress, running all REFUSE; a capitalized 'Executed' refuses (out of vocab); and a missing status refuses. The status vocabulary is proposal-only {proposed,superseded,withdrawn}, so the artifact structurally cannot say 'I ran it'. THE TWO SAFETY OMISSIONS: a missing rollback refuses; a missing required_authorization refuses; an out-of-vocab authorization refuses. THE TWO-KEY BINDING: reversibility.class irreversible OR data_mutating true forces required_authorization two_key or refuses - I confirmed irreversible-without-two_key REFUSES and data_mutating:true-without-two_key REFUSES; data_mutating:yes (truthy-looking non-bool) refuses (no silent truthy acceptance). POSITIVE CONTROLS pass clean: reversible+human_confirmation, irreversible+two_key, data_mutating:true+two_key, reversible+two_key (escalation allowed, nothing lowers), and costly+human_confirmation (costly is not the two-key trigger). All 12 adversarial unclaimed mutations I threw at it were refused; the contract has no way to encode 'and I executed it'.

.warp/incident.py reuses validate.parse_yamlish (no second parser) and validate.fail (no import cycle) exactly as decision.py and arch.py receive theirs - the caller injects them; incident.py imports only pathlib. It FAILS CLOSED by name on a wrong schema, a missing/empty required field, each out-of-vocabulary enum, a timeline with no opened_at, evidence with no citation, a proposed action with no action or parameters, and a file outside the parser subset (a tab-indented record refuses). bind_remedy fails closed when a remedy's incident does not resolve - I confirmed bind accepts a resolving incident (0) and refuses None (>0), and check_records refuses a remedy pointing at INC-GHOST (referenced but absent). ADOPTION SAFE: with no .warp/incidents/ AND no .warp/remedies/ directory check_records stands down and returns 0 (I confirmed over a temp tree); a required-but-absent single record fails closed; a present malformed record fails closed; and a duplicate incident id or remedy id within its set is refused. resolve_incident matches on schema AND id so a remedy-shaped file is never mistaken for an incident.

findings.text: FULL W1 SCOPE DELIVERED WITH NO DODGE, AND THE SAFETY INVARIANTS ARE REAL (the crux for this safety-critical plan). Both contracts carry every mandated field/behavior and every validation has teeth; the proposal-not-execution safety center holds under adversarial probing (12 unclaimed mutations refused, all positive controls pass). Unlike prior W-items caught dropping mandated behavior, nothing here is dropped or substituted. The artifact structurally cannot encode execution or skip rollback/authorization, and irreversible-or-data-mutating is force-bound to two_key so WARP-1207 (W7) has an exact binding.

VALIDATE.PY RESTORATION IS NOW NEEDED BEFORE THE PLAN-0012 RELEASES CAN WIRE THEIR CHECKS (flag for the orchestrator). validate.py at 1207 lines is over the 1000-line module_lines budget, and the now-live W2 shape gate REFUSES any change that touches it. run_all() is a linear sequence of hardcoded validator calls with no discovery/registry, so W11 (WARP-1211), which must 'land the checks in the canonical engine' by wiring check_records into run_all, is BLOCKED until validate.py is brought under budget. This is the exact entropy crossing PLAN-0011's W8/W9 restoration loop exists to draft a remedy for: a validate.py restoration (refactor/split it under 1000 lines, e.g. extracting the contract-validator loaders and run_all registration into a smaller module) should precede or be part of W11. This is not a W1 defect (W1 correctly deferred and did not touch the over-budget file), but the debt compounds across every future release that needs run_all wiring and should be scheduled deliberately rather than discovered at W11.

EXECUTION-CAPABILITY CHECK IS AN EXACT-KEY DENYLIST, so a novel narrative field outside the enumerated set is tolerated (not blocking). I confirmed a top-level 'executed_at: <ts>' field and a 'command:' key NESTED inside proposed_action.parameters are TOLERATED by validate_remedy (the check tests exact top-level keys against EXECUTION_CAPABILITY_FIELDS and only requires proposed_action.parameters to be a mapping). Neither defeats proposal-not-execution: (a) the authoritative structural state is the status field, which is locked to the proposal-only vocabulary and cannot claim execution; (b) an inert extra field grants no capability - the executor (W6) is a separate organ that acts only on a whitelisted action reference + validated parameters bound to a proposal digest + the authorization keys, and never reads proposal narrative, and free-form command text has no machine path (NG2); (c) this known-field posture matches the sibling validators decision.py and arch.py. Recommendation (hardening, not a W1 blocker): if a future item wants defense in depth, validate_remedy could reject unknown top-level keys, but the current design's safety rests correctly on the separate-organ architecture plus the closed status vocabulary plus the enumerated capability-field denylist, all of which hold.

INCIDENT.PY IS NOT ENUMERATED IN THE ARCHITECTURE CONTRACT'S AREA INCLUDES (identical to every prior placeless organ module, correct here). incident.py resolves to no declared area via arch.area_for_path, so it sits outside every shape-gate budget and is not itself measured - exactly as shape_gate.py, decision.py, arch.py, entropy.py, restoration.py, and the other .warp organ modules are already treated. This is CORRECT for W1: the spec's footprint does not include the human-approved .warp/architecture.yaml, so the builder rightly did not unilaterally expand the contract. Hygiene recommendation for a later human-approved contract revision: enumerate these .warp organ modules in their areas so they are governed and self-measured. Not a dropped W1 mandate and not blocking.
